tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web (pages, news, docs, blogs) and get up to 50 results with title, URL, date and a summary written for you to read. Use it first whenever you need to look something up: one call, $0.0009 per search, nothing when there are no results. Query operators: site:example.com (several: site:a.com

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Read one web page as clean Markdown (title and text, no menus or ads). Always use this, not browser_run, when you only need what a page says. For YouTube, Reddit, X, TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn, Google Maps or Amazon pages use suggest_tools and run_tool instead: they return the data itself (video de

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Create an image from a description with GPT Image 2.5 (GPT Image 2 as backup): illustrations, photos, product shots, posters, icons, diagrams with little text, UI mockups. Give reference images in `images` to edit a picture or to keep a product, logo, person or style the same. $0.04 per image, any s

tools.name: get_image
tools.description: An image from generate_image that was still being made: waits for it, then returns its download link. Free.

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Find data tools for a platform by describing what you need (Google Maps, TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn, Amazon, Reddit, X, YouTube, reviews, jobs…). Returns tool ids with prices. For plain web search use web_search.

tools.name: suggest_tools
tools.description: Describe the whole task (e.g. "find vegan restaurants in Austin and summarise their latest reviews", "get the transcript and top comments of this YouTube video") and get an ordered plan in ~0.5s: the tool to run first, an optional second tool, close alternatives, each with an example input to adapt

tools.name: get_tool
tools.description: A tool's input schema (field descriptions carry its query syntax), an example input and its price. Read it before run_tool unless suggest_tools already gave you example_input: run_tool rejects input that doesn't match the schema.

tools.name: run_tool
tools.description: Run a data tool (an id from suggest_tools or search_tools) and get its results. `input` must follow the tool's input_schema: start from suggest_tools' example_input or get_tool's example and change only the values. It waits for the results; a longer job answers with a run_id — then call get_run with

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: Status and results of a tool run: waits for it to finish, then returns its results compact. `offset` pages through the items; `fields` keeps only the keys you need. Free: use it to re-read a finished run with other fields instead of running the tool again.

tools.name: browser_run
tools.description: Run an AI browser agent on a website you have to interact with: log in, click through, fill and submit forms, multi-page flows. To read what a page says use web_fetch, to find pages use web_search: both are faster and cheaper. The browser runs in the cloud and cannot open localhost or private addres

tools.name: browser_status
tools.description: Status of a browser run (waits up to ~45s for progress). When status is waiting_for_human, "needs" says what it needs: a question to answer, an approval, or a takeover (live_view_url for the user).

tools.name: browser_reply
tools.description: Reply to a browser run waiting for a human: {"answer": "…"} for a question, {"approve": true|false} for an approval, {"done": true} after the user finished a takeover. Codes and passwords the user gives should be sent by them through the API "secret" reply, not through this tool.

tools.name: browser_takeover
tools.description: Ask a browser run to hand the browser to the user now; the run status then carries a live_view_url.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "browser_run" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: web_search, web_fetch, search_tools, suggest_tools, browser_run · Private data: web_fetch, generate_image, browser_run, browser_reply · Public sink: browser_run · Destructive: suggest_tools, run_tool, get_run, browser_run, browser_status, browser_reply, browser_takeover.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: web_search, web_fetch, search_tools, suggest_tools, browser_run · Private data: web_fetch, generate_image, browser_run, browser_reply · Public sink: browser_run · Destructive: suggest_tools, run_tool, get_run, browser_run, browser_status, browser_reply, browser_takeover

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
